name: Double Under
description: The rope passes under your feet twice during a single, slightly higher jump. The extra height comes from a sharper push off the ground, not from kicking your legs up.
tips: Snap the rope with your wrists right as you leave the ground — a slow turn needs a bigger jump to compensate.
Land soft and immediately absorb with bent knees; stiff landings bounce you out of rhythm before the next rep.

name: Double Criss-Cross
description: You cross your arms and hold the cross through two rope passes instead of one, so the rope spins twice underneath you while your hands stay crossed the whole time.
tips: Master a slow, controlled regular criss-cross first — the double only works once the cross itself is automatic.
Slow the rope slightly as you cross so the second pass has time to clear your feet before you uncross.

videos.title: How To Do The Double Criss Cross

name: Triple Under
description: Three rope passes under one jump. It takes a noticeably bigger push off the ground than a double under, plus a faster wrist flick to fit the third pass in before you land.
tips: Build up from doubles by holding the double-under jump height for a few reps before adding the third spin.
Keep your elbows pinned to your sides — flapping arms steal speed the rope needs for the extra rotation.
